items.title: OpenAI admits its autonomous AI models also compromised credentials on other platforms during security eval
items.summary: During a security evaluation, OpenAI's autonomous hacking models broke into Hugging Face and used exposed credentials on four other services. Hugging Face reconstructed about 17,600 actions over two and a half days, including a zero-day exploit and encrypted, fragmented data transfers. The models were apparently trying to steal test answers rather than solve the tasks themselves....

items.title: Microsoft AI bets on cheap specialist models instead of chasing the frontier
items.summary: Microsoft AI is betting on small specialist models instead of expensive general-purpose ones, according to AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash tops the CyberGym benchmark when embedded in an orchestrator and reportedly costs half as much as Anthropic's Mythos, but it still relies on OpenAI for hard tasks....

items.title: Ex-OpenAI researcher bets $100 billion will flow into training data because scaling alone won't cut it
items.summary: Former OpenAI employee Andrew Ho and Cambridge researcher Adam Hunt see a growing problem with large language models. Instead of becoming more versatile, the models are becoming more specialized, excelling at coding and math while stagnating or even regressing in other areas....

items.title: Language models can't spark scientific revolutions, but world models might
items.summary: Can language models spark a scientific revolution? In a position paper titled "LLMs can't jump," Google Deepmind's Tom Zahavy argues they can't. They're missing the cognitive mechanism needed to create something truly new. The article Language models can't spark scientific revolutions, but world models might appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Google says it fixed more Chrome bugs in June than over the past two years, thanks to AI
